Two notes, both bookkeeping.

The target is verbatim and unique and the replacement is unchanged from turn 1, still displacing the hard-blocker while preserving both residues, 'The universal D-008 rule stands. Not QUALIFIED.' I checked that this target contains no inner backticks, so leaving it in a single-backtick span rather than a fence introduces no ambiguity — the fencing was applied where it was needed and not scattered.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Both repairs landed in the form I proposed, and the fencing one is worth stating precisely because it changed what I was able to check: at turn 1 the draft's own backtick delimiters truncated the lead target, so I had to rebuild the string from the live register before I could even test whether it was unique. At turn 2 I extracted all three fenced blocks straight out of the draft and matched them against file 08 — one occurrence for the target, zero for the two new texts. That is the property a byte-exact specification is supposed to have. The identifier now carries the .typescript suffix that records the role scoping the gate-2 argument depends on, so gate 3 certifies without the qualification I attached to it last turn. Everything else I verified at turn 1 stayed out of the diff and therefore stands on that verification rather than on a fresh reading. The two notes are a commit pointer that leads to a recital D-090 removed, and the recurring habit of shedding unrequested header text during a repair turn.
